253458103_a4c3e9ae.text: For instance, histaminergic Hdc-positive neurons were mostly contained within the basal LH3, Nts (neurotensin)- and Tac2 (tachykinin 2)-expressing cells lie strictly within LH4, Hcrt (hypocretin/orexin)-positive and Pmch (pro-melanin-concentrating hormone)-positive neurons appeared within separate LH5 subdivisions

253458103_fd160d48.text: Hcrt cells occupy acroterminal and retrotuberal portions of our terminal LH5 subregion

253458103_ddcdf45f.text: The Hcrt and Pmch populations are associated to the more dorsal orexin and melanin-concentrating-hormone populations that have been reported in the LH (Broberger 1999; Brischoux et al. 2001; Elias et al. 1998). This molecularly identified population displayed a larger ventral extension than shown in preceding maps, likely due to the use here of highly sensitive in situ hybridization labeling. The Hcrt population extends caudally into the PHy region where it broadly overlaps with the Pmch population. This population reaches rostrally the ventral terminal subregion of the peduncular hypothalamus, where it acroterminally abuts on the terminal tuberal region rich in Pomc-positive and Cartpt-positive neurons, and also on the ventral terminal perimamillary/ periretromamillary region. The terminal Hcrt cells appear lateral to the ventral terminal Pmch population, but this differs from an opposite relation observed in the PHy area, where Hcrt neurons lie dorsal to Pmch neurons (Figs. 18, 19). The Hcrt-positive cells are mostly glutamatergic, according to the concurrent expression of Slc17a6 and Lhx9, and generally do not overlap with Pmch neurons, though these neighboring populations share expression of Nkx2.2 (Brischoux et al. 2001; Sheng et al. 2019).
